statusDetail: Coverage-complete report-mode audit. Representative public templates, search, login validation, localization and 404 recovery were covered. Authenticated favorites/profile/upload, sign-up completion, voting/comments, age-verification completion and external affiliate destinations were not covered because they require accounts, identity data, side effects or leave the first-party site.

page.framework: Server-rendered multi-page site with jQuery-enhanced interactions
page.notes: Public image catalogue with homepage taxonomy, category listings, gallery details, search-to-category routing, authentication, 16 localized homepages, a manifest and extensive XML sitemaps.

principleOutcomes.reason: No developer intent or agent-facing transaction surface was declared; this emerging capability is optional here. Public content is nevertheless exposed in semantic raw HTML and crawlable links. The audited browse, gallery and sign-in tasks have no clear need for on-device language-model or summarisation features.

paths.description: Homepage/category discovery template and primary browse entry; tested desktop, mobile, dark/reduced-motion, forced-colors, performance, network, accessibility and memory conditions.
Representative category/listing template, selected because it is the main route from homepage taxonomy into galleries.
Representative gallery/detail template, selected from the category page to cover content viewing, metadata, image delivery and actions.
Primary search journey using the homepage query form; the query resolved to a matching category route.
Authentication form template, including a blank submit to exercise validation and recovery without using credentials.
Spanish localized homepage, selected to check translated content, lang metadata and CSS internationalisation readiness.
Representative HTTP error/recovery surface using a nonexistent route.

findings.summary: The manual theme control does not follow the operating-system color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark/reduced-motion screenshot remains the same light surface as the default screenshot; computed color-scheme is normal and the stylesheet probe found zero prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and drive surface/text tokens from prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), while keeping the manual override as an explicit user choice.

findings.summary: Route and major state changes use abrupt document swaps rather than View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS feature probe found zero view-transition rules and recon found no authored View Transition rules on homepage, category, or detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation and same-document transitions for major state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Very long listing pages provide no scroll-state-aware navigation or progress cue.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout measured 108,770 CSS px of content, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state queries, scroll timelines, or progress treatment; the header does not remain as responsive chrome during the long browse.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact sticky header and/or progress affordance that reacts declaratively to scroll state without obscuring content.

findings.summary: A fixed consent banner obscures content in the first viewport on every tested public template.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the cookie notice fixed over the lower content; the DOM probe measured it as a full-width fixed overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the banner footprint, preserve equal Accept/Reject choices, and move detailed preferences into a light-dismissible secondary surface.

findings.summary: The fixed consent surface is an ad-hoc div rather than an explicit semantic overlay/banner primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM recon found no dialog or popover elements; the fixed cookie surface is a div with custom behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an appropriately labelled semantic region for the non-modal banner and a native dialog/popover for detailed preferences, preserving keyboard focus and Escape/light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is entirely viewport-based rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The live stylesheet probe found zero @container rules despite reusable cards, headers, forms and grid components appearing in different widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable layout components and size/content container queries where component behavior currently depends on page-wide breakpoints.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly exposed on key controls and some targets are too small.
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus showed outline:none and no box shadow on the search input, search button and menu button; the probe also found a 22px-wide random control and many 19px-tall links.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible treatment and increase compact interactive hit areas to at least 24 CSS px, preferably 44px for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP misses the good Core Web Vitals range under standard Lighthouse throttling.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.6s, FCP 3.1s and Speed Index 5.3s (performance 0.70); an unthrottled trace was better at 1.893s, so the slow-network/mobile path is the failure condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the first content image, reduce its render delay, remove critical-path CSS delay, and validate under repeatable mobile throttling until LCP is under 2.5s.

findings.summary: Critical CSS and unoptimised images delay meaningful content.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified 890ms estimated render-blocking savings and a 1,729ms LCP element render delay; HAR recorded 978KB initial transfer with 503KB images, while image delivery showed about 360KB potential savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline or split critical CSS, defer non-critical CSS, add fetchpriority=high to the LCP image, and serve responsive AVIF/WebP variants.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 224KiB unused JavaScript and 28KiB unused CSS; the main bundle was 57.6% unused, Google Identity 75.0%, jQuery 68.5%, and one secondary stylesheet 97.0%.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by route/feature, load identity code only when authentication is requested, remove obsolete jQuery dependencies, and purge or split unused CSS.

findings.summary: Some image links in the age-information surface have no accessible name.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility found two linked certification images with no alt text; both parent links therefore have no discernible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Give informative linked images concise alt text or label the links directly; use empty alt only when the link has another accessible name.

findings.summary: Several text/link combinations fail WCAG contrast minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found footer text at 2.92:1 and multiple pink links on the age-information background at 3.63:1, below the required 4.5:1 for normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground or background tokens to meet at least 4.5:1 for normal text and verify all theme/high-contrast states.

findings.summary: Visible keyboard focus is missing on primary controls.
findings.evidence: The focus-walk probe reported outline:none and no compensating box-shadow for the search input, search button and menu button, making keyboard location unclear.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a consistent, high-contrast :focus-visible ring to every interactive element and test the complete tab order on desktop and mobile layouts.

findings.summary: The viewport scale and compact targets weaken zoom/touch usability.
findings.evidence: The viewport is initial-scale=0.8, Lighthouse flagged mobile viewport optimisation, and the target probe found controls/links below 24px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Use initial-scale=1, keep user scaling unrestricted, and enlarge compact hit areas without harming reflow.

findings.summary: The homepage logs an identity-provider error for signed-out visitors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded the console error “Not signed in with the identity provider.” during an ordinary anonymous load.
findings.suggestedFix: Only initialise the identity provider when needed and handle the signed-out state without logging an error.

findings.summary: A small set of certification images lacks explicit dimensions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse and the detail image audit found the ASACP and RTA images without width/height attributes, even though the main content imagery reserves space correctly.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width and height attributes (or an equivalent aspect-ratio reservation) to every image.

findings.summary: The large first-party JavaScript bundle has no valid production source map.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported that pornpics.js, a roughly 233KB transferred first-party bundle, is missing a source map.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a correctly referenced source map for the production bundle, or provide secure authenticated maps to monitoring/debug tooling.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are incomplete and inconsistent across public templates.
findings.evidence: Homepage recon found no canonical URL or hreflang links; the Spanish page also had no hreflang, while the representative public gallery sends noindex,follow despite being reachable from category pages. Robots points to a working multilingual sitemap index.
findings.suggestedFix: Add self-referencing canonicals and reciprocal hreflang clusters; review gallery noindex policy and align it deliberately with the multilingual/image sitemaps.

findings.summary: Gallery detail pages expose neither structured entity data nor social preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The representative gallery has a descriptive title/H1 but no JSON-LD and no Open Graph properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org ImageGallery/ImageObject or CreativeWork JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata that matches the visible page.

findings.summary: A permissive CSP and insecure cookies weaken an otherwise HTTPS/HSTS transport posture.
findings.evidence: Headers show CSP default-src * data: blob: unsafe-inline unsafe-eval; cookies reported all five first-party cookies without Secure, including g_state with SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the wildcard CSP with explicit origins and nonces/hashes, remove unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline where possible, and mark HTTPS-only cookies Secure with the narrowest suitable SameSite policy.

findings.summary: Authentication offers password and federated login but no phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: Login recon shows username/password fields and Google sign-in with correct autocomplete tokens, but no WebAuthn/passkey capability was exposed; no permission prompts fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration and conditional authentication as a progressive option, retaining recovery and existing sign-in methods.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are absent or too weak.
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS but omit X-Content-Type-Options and Permissions-Policy; clickjacking protection relies on a broad frame-ancestors allowlist, and Referrer-Policy remains no-referrer-when-downgrade.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, tighten frame-ancestors, use strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy, and evaluate Trusted Types for the script-heavy surface.

findings.summary: Localized pages set lang correctly but the shared CSS is not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: The Spanish page correctly uses lang=es and translated content, but stylesheet inspection found zero logical box properties versus 246 physical margin/padding/border declarations and 60 left/right declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace physical directional properties with logical inline/block equivalents and test RTL/writing-mode variants; add dir where language context requires it.

findings.summary: The image-heavy experience sends legacy, non-responsive assets at avoidable cost.
findings.evidence: Homepage image audit found 96 legacy-format images, 97 without srcset, 93 below-fold images without native lazy loading and four oversized; the detail template had 21 legacy images, 23 without srcset and nine oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, supply width-based srcset/sizes, preserve dimensions, prioritise only above-fold content, and lazy-load below-fold images with native loading.

taskList.title: Modernise responsive image delivery and LCP prioritisation
Harden CSP, cookies and browser security policies
Restore accessible names, contrast, focus and touch/zoom behavior
Split unused JavaScript/CSS and defer identity code
Add canonical, hreflang, structured data and share metadata
Respect the system theme while preserving the manual override
Reduce and semantically rebuild the consent surface
Adopt component and scroll-state responsive patterns
Make localized layout CSS writing-mode resilient
Add passkey authentication as a progressive option

No authored View Transition rules were found for route/state changes.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No known tracker origins or exposed secrets were found; the only external runtime origin was Google Identity for an offered sign-in path.

nosniff and Permissions-Policy are missing; frame/referrer/CSP policies are broad.

The mobile menu interaction completed without clipping/crash, standard links remained usable, and no runtime blank state appeared.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline/post heap summaries and same-session metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: After 10 full-page scroll cycles, DOM element count was unchanged; heap snapshot size rose about 4.8% while lazy content was exercised, and closure count slightly decreased, providing no evidence of unbounded retained growth in this window.
Baseline heap self-size was about 10.1MB with 158,828 heap nodes, proportionate to a long image grid; rendered DOM contained 1,161 elements.

checkOutcomes.method: Before/after heap constructor comparison and DOM metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: No Detached constructor appeared among the dominant heap constructors, rendered DOM count stayed unchanged after repetition, and closure count fell from 6,207 to 6,198.
